primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II due to SEC23B deficiency
mechanism: SEC23B is a component of the COPII coat that mediates export of newly synthesized proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum toward the Golgi. Biallelic SEC23B defects impair erythroid maturation and protein trafficking/processing, causing congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II with ineffective erythropoiesis and characteristic binucleated erythroblasts.
vignette: A 12-year-old boy has lifelong anemia, intermittent jaundice, splenomegaly, and increasing serum ferritin despite few transfusions. Bone marrow examination shows erythroid hyperplasia with numerous binucleated erythroblasts. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SEC23B.
lead: The affected protein normally participates most directly in which of the following cellular processes?
correct: COPII-mediated transport of newly synthesized proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus
distractors: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis from the plasma membrane
Mannose-6-phosphate tagging of lysosomal enzymes in the Golgi apparatus
Import of nuclear proteins through nuclear pore complexes
Ubiquitin-dependent degradation of proteins by the proteasome
distractor_notes: SEC23B is a secretory COPII-coat component rather than a clathrin endocytic component.
Mannose-6-phosphate tagging is performed by Golgi-resident enzymes and is not the direct function of SEC23B.
Nuclear import uses importins and nuclear-pore transport machinery rather than COPII coat proteins.
Proteasomal degradation uses ubiquitin-proteasome machinery, whereas SEC23B functions in secretory vesicle trafficking.
key_expl: SEC23B is a core COPII coat component required for ER-to-Golgi transport. Its deficiency selectively disrupts erythroid maturation and causes CDA II, characterized by ineffective erythropoiesis, binucleated erythroblasts, splenomegaly, jaundice, and iron overload.
objective: Link SEC23B-related congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II to defective COPII-mediated ER-to-Golgi protein transport.
